title: Infinitary logic: countable conjunctions and compactness boundaries
summary: Well-founded countable formulas express infinity and the standard successor domain, while finite satisfiability no longer guarantees a model.
abstract: An infinite first-order theory can require arbitrarily many distinct elements, but no single ordinary first-order sentence expresses an infinite domain. Allowing countable conjunctions turns that theory into one sentence, which can then be negated. We define the enlarged syntax with finite free-variable contexts and well-founded formula trees, retain the usual quantifier semantics, and prove that ordinary formulas embed without changing truth. Countable connectives express both infinity and the assertion that every element is a finite successor of zero. An explicit countable theory has a finite model for every finite subset and no model for the whole theory, showing exactly where ordinary compactness stops applying.
